messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to prioritize the customer migration gracepath epic. A few key enterprise customers asked for: extended pin TTLs, per-tenant rollback tokens, and clearer canary/launch criteria. Can we decide scope for Q2?
Alex: Can you list the exact acceptance criteria customers want? and which ones are blockers vs nice-to-have?
Jordan: From CS: BigCorp asked specifically for 90-day pin window (instead of our default 30d), a soft-fallback to previous model during errors, and a migration audit log they can hand to compliance. They said we must avoid breaking SDK behavior.
Sam: Technical constraints: extending pin TTL is straightforward in catalog metadata but per-tenant override means routing + auth checks on each request -> latency risk. We should quantify p95 impact. Also need canary gates: p50/stddev token time, p95 latency delta < 20%, and output-delta checks.
Priya: Legal/security: per-tenant rollback tokens implies token lifecycle and KMS storage. Need to scope whether tokens are short-lived or perpetual and whether we store them encrypted in our control plane.
Maya: Proposed MVP scope for Q2 (exit criteria):
 - Opt-in pin TTL extension to 90d (catalog flag + UI toggle)
 - Canary rollout API: per-customer canary route that supports weight and fallback
 - Migration audit log (append-only, exportable CSV)
Launch criteria: docs + SDK bump, runbook for manual rollback, e2e canary at >=2 customers.
Alex: Resource ask: 2 FE days (UI), 3 BE days (routing + flags), 4 infra days (canary infra + metrics). If we phase, do TTL + audit first, then canary API.
Sam: For canary success signals I propose a minimal JSON to codify checks. Paste below for engineering review:
```
{
  "canary_window_minutes": 60,
  "traffic_weight": 0.05,
  "checks": {
    "latency_p95_delta_pct": 20,
    "error_rate_increase_pct": 50,
    "semantic_similarity_drop": 0.12
  },
  "rollback_on_failure": true
}
```
Jordan: Customers will want an SLA on rollback time. They asked for <= 15min for automated fallback and <= 60min for manual rollback. Also they want a clear comms template for deprecations.
Priya: For tokens: propose HSM-backed short-lived tokens (valid 24h) plus a one-click emergency rollback token stored encrypted per-tenant (requires legal sign-off).
Maya: Trade-offs: shorter tokens = better security but more ops for customers. Phased plan seems safest: Q2a = TTL + audit + docs; Q2b = canary API + SDK + rollout UI; Q3 = per-tenant long-lived opt-in tokens + legal/compliance package.
Alex: Sounds good. One engineering ask: add a non-blocking telemetry tag when a request uses an overridden pin so we can track usage and perf.
Sam: Agreed. We should also add a synthetic eval step during canary: run our eval harness on a small prompt set and flag semantic regression > threshold. That ties to the semantic_similarity_drop check.
Jordan: I'll draft a customer comms template and a short opt-in contract amendment. Will share by EOD Friday.
Maya: Action items: @Alex scope FE/BE tickets, @Sam prototype canary checks + telemetry, @Priya list compliance requirements for tokens, @Jordan comms + customer sign-off path. We'll review on Wed sync.
